career_arrival_01.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_01.text: The employment notices reached Reed Crossing in a covered basket, beside a repaired sandal and three letters that had missed the morning carrier. Yue had expected a summons to another emergency. Instead the receiving clerk asked whether she wanted work that could still exist after the emergency ended. She read the question twice. Her training book contained places she had helped and places she had left. It contained no answer about where she wanted to become ordinary.

career_arrival_02.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_02.text: The clerk cleared a dry corner of the receiving table. None of the new offers drew money from the crossing's settled recovery account. The grain, linen and private wage accounts remained filed under their actual dates and results. A new appointment could give Yue a livelihood. It could not purchase a better version of the ferry journey.

career_arrival_03.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_03.text: Beside the notices, someone had drawn a little ladder. The lowest rung said learner; the next said accepted work; the highest had been left blank. Yue traced the blank with one finger. She had imagined advancement as leaving the lower rungs behind. The sandal's owner arrived and asked for a needle. Without thinking, she helped him find one before returning to the ladder.

career_arrival_04.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_04.text: The clerk gave her the offers' named contacts rather than a recommendation. The kiln wanted an experienced worker willing to learn a narrower inspection role. The archive wanted a reader willing to accept supervision in condition recording. The survey team wanted a measurer willing to have her own maps corrected. None asked for a celebrated rescuer.

career_arrival_05.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_05.text: Yue set her fifth-stage record on the table. The clerk read the examiner's scope and returned it. It described four stable pairs under the accepted trial conditions. It described neither a conservator's authority nor a surveyor's right to open a closed road. Yue had brought it because it mattered to her. It was useful to see exactly where it stopped mattering to another person's decision.

career_arrival_06.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_06.text: A carrier waiting at the rail asked whether she could take all three places and send assistants to two. The clerk shook her head. Each induction required her own attendance, practice and review. The teams had offered one place to one named learner. An assistant's work would need an assistant's contract.

career_arrival_07.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_07.text: Yue laughed before she could stop herself. She had recognized her own temptation in the carrier's question. She could make three good arguments for going; she could make none for being in three rooms. The clerk moved the notices apart so their dates could be seen without covering one another.

career_arrival_08.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_08.text: The kiln notice bore Peng Ai's careful hand. It recognized Yue's earlier labor and the failed firings she had helped retain. Returning would not erase those records or reopen the teaching season she had previously declined. The offered inspection trial was a new, narrower contract. She pictured the kiln wall warm through her sleeves.

career_arrival_09.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_09.text: Tan Ke's archive notice had a thumbprint of paste beside the fold. Past reading work could help a trainee learn. It did not qualify that trainee to treat damaged paper. The offered appointment began with observing and recording condition under supervision, and ended with a bounded independent review. Yue pictured a page she had once wanted to rescue by touching it too quickly.

career_arrival_10.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_10.text: The survey offer came with an ordinary sketch of a cleared drainage path. Yuan's field shifts and the independent recorder review had their own small budget. The task concerned measurements and what their maps could support. Structural clearance remained with the actual bridge examiner. Yue pictured the river after the second bell, when every neat line had seemed too small.

career_arrival_11.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_11.text: She asked how long she could consider the notices. Until the named receiving hour, the clerk said. After that, unused places would return to the ordinary list. No team had bought a promise by sending an offer. Yue looked at the ladder again and found that this limit made it easier to breathe.

career_arrival_12.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_12.text: The sandal's owner left his repaired shoe on the floor while he tested the stitching with his other foot. He asked which job sounded most impressive. Yue could not answer. Which work could she bear to have checked on a tired morning, after her first good result had stopped being new? The clerk smiled at that question without choosing for her.

career_arrival_13.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_13.text: Before sunset she made a list of what she could already do, what required help and what she wanted to learn. Under the third heading she wrote steady work. She crossed it out, embarrassed by its smallness, then wrote it again. The paper was hers. Nobody had required a grander ambition.

career_arrival_14.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_14.text: A wage claimant came to collect a permitted case copy. His dispute still needed evidence through the ordinary wage desk. Yue made room at the table. He asked whether her next job would finish his case. She gave him the wage desk's contact and its stated queue. Employment at a different institution could not make that promise true.

career_arrival_15.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_15.text: After he left, Yue folded her ambitions around the three notices. She did not want every unfinished question to become a reason she could never begin a life of her own. She also did not want a new name to make those questions disappear. Between those wishes lay a smaller task: accept one scope and perform it.

career_arrival_16.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_16.text: The clerk offered an ordinary day-work register as a fourth option. Yue could decline all three appointments and keep her name available for separate short contracts. That choice offered flexibility and uncertain hours, without a specialist qualification. She would not lose the stage, practice or pay she had already earned.

career_arrival_17.speaker: narrator
career_arrival_17.text: She carried the notices to the terrace rail. The depth rod was back on its rack; the river had no interest in her decision. On the far bank, a worker brought a covered bowl to someone finishing a late shift. Yue watched the two of them make space on a narrow bench. For the first time that day, she pictured a future smaller than a rescue and larger than a departure.

career_entry.speaker: narrator
career_entry.text: After the crossing's final receiving, Yue stayed above the flood line for the next ordinary post. Her earlier cargo decision, the settled recovery service and the unresolved bridge question retained their own accounts. This morning brought three employment offers, each with a named supervisor and a place for one learner. She had time to choose a livelihood without pretending that choosing it would finish every obligation behind her.

career_enrol_choice.speaker: lin_yue
career_enrol_choice.text: I can accept one supervised appointment, or leave the specialist places for other applicants and seek separate day work. Each appointment pays for performed work and requires its own review before advancement. My fifth stage remains earned; it does not appoint me. I want to choose work I can learn, including the parts I will get wrong.

choices.text: Join the kiln's paid inspection training.
Join the archive's paid condition-record training.
Join the watershed team's paid survey-record training.
Decline these appointments and take independent day work.

career_independent_02.speaker: narrator
career_independent_02.text: The first request was modest: sort damaged packing cloth at the upper store after its ordinary inspection had cleared entry. The owner offered four copper for one morning and supplied the table and gloves. Yue asked who would decide whether the sorting was finished. He named the receiving keeper, who would count the accepted bundles in her presence.

career_independent_03.speaker: narrator
career_independent_03.text: She waited a day before the request was confirmed. Nobody paid her for that waiting, and she had not agreed to reserve it without compensation. She ate from her own provisions and let another short job pass while she considered its unsafe carrying terms. Flexibility had a price she could feel without declaring it punishment.

career_independent_04.speaker: narrator
career_independent_04.text: At the cleared store, Yue found that two labels had washed to the same pale mark. She put those bundles aside for the owner rather than inventing their old destinations. The receiving keeper checked them against the remaining inventory. The hour she spent doing this belonged to the agreed sorting shift, not an extra favor hidden outside it.

career_independent_05.speaker: narrator
career_independent_05.text: By midday the keeper accepted eight usable packing bundles and six for rag recovery. Two remained disputed. Yue's completed scope was sorting and condition recording; it did not include deciding the disputed ownership. The owner paid the agreed four copper with a receipt naming the performed morning. No specialist credential was issued.

career_independent_06.speaker: narrator
career_independent_06.text: Yue bought a bowl of noodles for one copper and put the other three away. At the stall, a young worker asked why she had declined training if she was willing to sort cloth. She said she wanted to keep her next months open. He said he wanted a timetable he could trust. They ate beside one another without making either answer universal.

career_independent_07.speaker: narrator
career_independent_07.text: The keeper asked whether Yue would stay for a second morning. Yue declined because she had promised to attend the next ordinary receiving and consider work closer to home. The keeper hired someone else at the same stated rate. Leaving after an agreed finish was different from leaving a half-sorted room and calling the departure freedom.

career_independent_08.speaker: narrator
career_independent_08.text: In her training book, Yue recorded the checked sorting result and the unresolved bundles. She retained no authority over another worker's later findings. The small account would let her show actual completed work when seeking another contract. It would not let her describe herself as a qualified kiln inspector, archive recorder or survey recorder.

career_independent_09.speaker: narrator
career_independent_09.text: She slept that night without a specialist appointment waiting for her. The uncertainty was real. So was the relief of having made a choice she could explain without borrowing the dignity of a profession she had not joined. In the morning she packed the repaired hem of her coat around her practice book and went to the named receiving.

career_independent_entry.speaker: narrator
career_independent_entry.text: Yue returned all three specialist notices before the receiving hour and entered her name on the ordinary day-work list. The clerk wrote no failure beside it. An available specialist place would go to its next applicant. Her choice had preserved time to travel and surrendered the certainty of those paid training schedules.

career_reunion_01.speaker: narrator
career_reunion_01.text: At the next appointed receiving, Yue put her completed work record on the dry table. The clerk compared the named finishes with the sources each institution had permitted her to carry. Other applicants were waiting behind her. Her future would have to fit into the same ordinary hours as theirs.

career_reunion_02.speaker: narrator
career_reunion_02.text: The old crossing folders remained on their own shelf. No new qualification reopened the freight ledger; no new earnings restored an annotation washed from its wrapper. Yue recognized the shelf by the torn edge of its label. She was glad the clerk had not moved it somewhere celebratory for her return.

career_reunion_03.speaker: narrator
career_reunion_03.text: Someone had filled in the ladder's highest rung with the words next responsibility. Yue read them and thought of the first mistake she had made in her chosen work. A title could help people find the right worker. If it hid what the worker could still get wrong, it would make the next room less safe.

career_reunion_04.speaker: narrator
career_reunion_04.text: The clerk turned to the part of the record supported by Yue's selected appointment. Where no specialist enrollment was recorded, the ordinary day-work receiving could state only ordinary completed work. It would not infer a profession from her scores or her older reputation. Yue waited while the clerk opened the correct portfolio.

career_portfolio_kiln_01.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_kiln_01.text: The kiln record named the supervised work, the retained failed attempt and the witnessed review. Yue could present the qualification within the scope actually accepted there. The clerk did not broaden it to every vessel, every kiln or another employer's test. The chosen specialty and its limits remained written in the source record she carried.

career_portfolio_kiln_02.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_kiln_02.text: She placed that record beside her older cultivation examination. Both mattered. They answered different questions. A customer could ask what inspection she was qualified to perform; a practice examiner could ask what channel trial she had passed. Neither paper needed to swallow the other for her to have become more capable.

career_portfolio_kiln_03.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_kiln_03.text: The clerk asked whether Yue wanted to request another bounded term, take time at home or return to separate day work. Her paid training was already finished. The next decision concerned future availability, without an unpaid tail attached to the completed contract. Yue touched the worn edge of the kiln record before answering.

career_portfolio_archive_01.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_archive_01.text: The archive record named the condition work Yue had performed and the bounded recording qualification she had earned through review. It authorized the accepted recording scope, not paper treatment, ownership or disclosure. Her selected specialty kept its actual findings and limitations. The original papers remained with their custodians.

career_portfolio_archive_02.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_archive_02.text: The clerk asked whether her title meant she could settle a damaged inheritance page. Yue said she could record its observable condition under the accepted scope and refer questions outside it. A record of loss did not decide an inheritance. She had learned to say this without feeling that the limit made the useful part smaller.

career_portfolio_archive_03.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_archive_03.text: Her training wages and completed handover had their own receipts. A later term would need later acceptance. The clerk offered a place to request it, an ordinary return home or separate day work. Yue thought of the first page she had observed without touching and the strange patience it had required.

career_portfolio_survey_01.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_survey_01.text: The survey portfolio named the field shifts, corrected failed map and independent recorder review. Yue could produce records within the accepted scope and describe the specialty she had actually completed. She could not turn the record into structural clearance, a land boundary judgment or an account of measurements nobody had taken.

career_portfolio_survey_02.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_survey_02.text: The clerk laid an old crossing sketch beside her new record and asked whether one replaced the other. Yue shook her head. The old sketch belonged to its observed time and conditions. The new field work had its own interval. A worker could improve without improving the past by changing its caption.

career_portfolio_survey_03.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_survey_03.text: The performed shifts and specialty work had been settled from their own survey budget. The clerk offered a request for another limited term, a return home or separate day work. Yue imagined walking a familiar path after enough rain to make it unfamiliar. She could want that work and still have to ask whether its next terms were acceptable.

career_portfolio_independent_01.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_independent_01.text: The ordinary portfolio could state only work supported by actual receiving records. Where the packing-cloth receipt was present, its accepted counts and disputed bundles retained their limits. Without a specialist enrollment record, the qualification lines stayed blank. The clerk would not fill them from Yue's reputation or infer a performed contract from her scores.

career_portfolio_independent_02.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_independent_02.text: Yue looked at the blank lines without filling them in. Leaving specialist appointments unrecorded did not supply their missing tests. A later application would need an actual available place and an honest account of prior experience. Where ordinary completed work was documented, it could support that application within its own scope.

career_portfolio_independent_03.speaker: narrator
career_portfolio_independent_03.text: The clerk could receive a request for another ordinary contract, list a period away or leave her name available for separate day work. Yue did not owe the register continuous availability because it had once helped her find a morning. She opened her practice book to a page on which she could make a new promise.

career_next_choice.speaker: lin_yue
career_next_choice.text: The work I accepted has reached its named finish. I can request a new limited term in my chosen field, take time at home, or seek separate day work. A request still needs the receiving team's acceptance. None of these choices earns another wage or grants another qualification before the work.

choices.text: Request another limited term in the selected line of work.
Take a period at home after the completed handover.
Keep specialist records and return to separate day work.

career_renew_dispatch.speaker: narrator
career_renew_dispatch.text: The clerk prepared a request addressed to the institution in Yue's selected enrollment record. The request carried the permitted qualification scope and her proposed availability. If no specialist enrollment was recorded, it went to the ordinary work register. No wages, materials or future places changed hands with the envelope.

career_renew_kiln_01.speaker: narrator
career_renew_kiln_01.text: Yue addressed the request to the kiln's receiving desk. She put the accepted specialty beside the tasks she proposed and left tasks outside that scope for other workers. The next placement and rate required the kiln's response and a new agreement. She retained the wages already paid and the limits already examined.

career_renew_kiln_02.speaker: narrator
career_renew_kiln_02.text: Yue kept one copy of the request and packed her practice book. A place at the kiln had become something she could ask to continue, with reasons grounded in performed work. She could picture a morning there without needing it to prove the value of every morning that preceded it.

career_renew_archive_01.speaker: narrator
career_renew_archive_01.text: Yue's application requested a later condition-record term at the archive. It left the next materials, hours and supervision for a new agreement before work began. Original custody and private permissions stayed with their actual keepers. She retained her completed qualification and paid work record while awaiting a response to the future placement request.

career_renew_archive_02.speaker: narrator
career_renew_archive_02.text: Yue watched the carrier put her envelope into an ordinary basket. A career could begin with a permitted record and continue through another agreement. She did not need to seize a damaged page to prove that she meant to return. Her hands were empty as she walked down the terrace steps.

career_renew_survey_01.speaker: narrator
career_renew_survey_01.text: Yue addressed the request for another recorder term to the survey team's receiving desk. New weather, access and work conditions would need their own checks and budget. Her accepted qualification did not guarantee a safe next path. It made the request specific enough for a supervisor to answer.

career_renew_survey_02.speaker: narrator
career_renew_survey_02.text: At the rail she drew the receiving table in the corner of her notebook, then crossed out the line where she had guessed its unseen leg. She could wait to observe that part. The little correction pleased her more than a flawless drawing would have. There was work she wanted to do again.
career_renew_survey_02.ending: A Map With Room to Correct

career_renew_independent_01.speaker: narrator
career_renew_independent_01.text: The ordinary work register received Yue's request for a short contract. It promised no specialist place and no wages for waiting. The clerk would send actual terms when a suitable request arrived. Any earlier work receipts retained their own dates and scopes; the new envelope added no completed shift to them.

career_renew_independent_02.speaker: narrator
career_renew_independent_02.text: She bought a fresh needle with her own money and mended the seam that had annoyed her for weeks. An open schedule did not become an easy life by being chosen. It did become a life whose next obligation could still be read before she accepted it.

career_home_01.speaker: narrator
career_home_01.text: Yue gave the clerk a period during which she would not accept new shifts. Her completed records stayed available under their actual permissions. She had finished the work before making the travel plan. No institution would have to guess whether she had simply failed to appear.

career_home_02.speaker: narrator
career_home_02.text: On the upper public road she passed a carrier with a wrapped bowl and thought of the narrow bench across the river. She wanted to arrive somewhere before her next task did. The wish felt ordinary enough to keep. Her earned stage and accepted work scopes travelled with her, without obliging her to spend every hour demonstrating them.
career_home_02.ending: A Finished Term and a Road Home

career_daywork_01.speaker: narrator
career_daywork_01.text: Yue kept the accepted specialist record where her chosen appointment had produced one, and asked the clerk to list her for separate short contracts. A former trainee could do ordinary work without discarding the qualification she had earned. A worker without that qualification could ask for the same ordinary terms honestly.

career_daywork_02.speaker: narrator
career_daywork_02.text: Before leaving she looked at the employment ladder one last time. Someone had drawn a chair beside it. She liked that addition. Work could ask her to become more capable; rest could ask nothing. She folded the next blank page of her practice book under the cover and stepped into the evening.
